draft.title: Report both score presence and value
draft.statement: Implement lookup_entry(scores, name, fallback). Return exactly an object with two keys: found is a JSON boolean that is true if and only if name is a key in scores; value is scores[name] when present and fallback otherwise. A present zero stays zero. A present value can equal fallback, so the value alone does not tell you whether the key exists. Inputs are valid JSON: scores is an object of integer values (not booleans), name is a string and fallback is an integer. Key matching is exact and case-sensitive. Do not mutate scores. Return the object; do not print it.

constraints: scores has at most 1000 string keys and integer values; booleans are excluded.
Return exactly found (boolean) and value (integer), with no extra keys.
found represents key membership, not value truthiness or comparison with fallback.
Do not mutate scores. Return-value checks do not certify non-mutation.

rubric.criterion: Distinguish presence independently from the returned value; preserve stored zeroes and caller fallback semantics. Return an exact boolean found flag and integer value.
rubric.family_rule: Presence reporting adds an observable decision absent from value-only lookup. Equal returned values for present and absent keys require different found flags; see the private S017 family audit. New family metadata alone grants no eligibility.
rubric.limits: Finite cases and root object checks do not establish arbitrary nested semantic correctness, non-mutation, complexity or unaided mastery. Actual assistance/familiarity and future evidence policy still apply.

examples.explanation: The key exists; report true and its stored value.
The key is absent; report false and the caller fallback.

assistance_steps.content: Treat existence and the chosen return value as two separate facts. Equal values can come from different presence states.
Use membership to obtain a boolean presence fact, then choose the stored value or caller fallback. Do not infer membership from truthiness or the chosen value.
If the name exists, return an object with found true and its stored score. Otherwise, return found false and the fallback.
Inside lookup_entry, branch on `name in scores`. In the present branch use `scores[name]` with found true; in the missing branch use fallback with found false.
The complete implementation reports key membership and selects the value in the same branch. Neither zero nor equality with fallback changes membership.

solution.explanation: Membership is independent from the stored value. A present zero and a present value equal to fallback both require found true; an absent key requires found false. Each branch selects the corresponding value without modifying scores.
solution.expected_complexity: Expected O(1) lookup time and O(1) extra space; reviewed, not certified by finite execution tests.

incorrect_solutions.label: PRESENCE_FROM_VALUE
PRESENCE_FROM_TRUTHINESS
incorrect_solutions.source_code:
def lookup_entry(scores, name, fallback):
    return {"found": bool(scores.get(name)), "value": scores.get(name, fallback)}

incorrect_solutions.label: FALSEY_VALUE_FALLBACK
incorrect_solutions.source_code:
def lookup_entry(scores, name, fallback):
    return {"found": name in scores, "value": scores.get(name) or fallback}
